whatis.intro: Product pricing is choosing what a case sells for. The price has to clear what the case costs you and stay close to what the account could pay elsewhere. For a distributor, a pricing rule decides where in that range each case lands.

cards.title: The floor is your cost
cards.body: Nothing sells below landed cost for long. In the calculator's example the floor is $22.00 a case, and every rule's margin is measured from it.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for the cost floor under every price

cards.title: The ceiling is the account's other option
cards.body: A competitor at $31.00 sets the price your account compares you against. Reliable delivery can stretch that ceiling a little, not remove it.
cards.alt: Magnifying glass, for the competitor price that caps a case

cards.title: The rule picks a spot in between
cards.body: Here the room between cost and the market is $9.00 a case. The rule you choose decides how much of it you keep and how much you give up to hold the account.
cards.alt: Slider controls, for the room between cost and the market

who.h2: Who uses a product pricing calculator
who.intro: Independent distributors that set their own prices use it to weigh one case against several pricing rules. Anyone who quotes a case, answers a rival quote or adds a new line should run it before the price goes out.

look.h2: Feed the pricing rules honest numbers first
look.intro: Each rule is only as honest as the numbers you feed it. A rep quoting off the result is trusting all three of these.

steps.title: A competitor price that is like for like
steps.body: A $31.00 quote may be a different pack, a different brand or a one-week deal. Match only the same case on the same delivery terms.

steps.title: Rebates counted only once they are earned
steps.body: Leave a supplier rebate out of the $22.00 unless you are sure to earn it. Miss the volume target and every case was priced off a cost lower than the one you paid.

steps.title: Volume that holds at the price
steps.body: The $51,360 a month assumes all 6,000 cases still sell at $30.56. If a raise costs you accounts, the real month is smaller.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits in your pricing
vos.h3: The price you choose is the price they order at
vos.body: VOS does not set or calculate your prices. It carries yours onto the order. Each account has its own order guide at the prices you set, and orders from it by voice in the VOS app.
bullets: Guides updated in one admin platform when you reprice
Each item tied to your own SKUs
Each app order arrives confirmed, with a number and a timestamp
Most distributors are live in 24 to 48 hours
